annotationRationale: The main task combines independent, nonuniform placements with an infinite sum over arithmetic progressions. The alternative uses the distribution's shift property to form a probability recurrence.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is correct; no subject repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The bin probabilities sum to one. Each favorable set is uniquely a,a+d,a+2d with a,d≥1, giving probability 6(∑8⁻ᵃ)(∑8⁻ᵈ)=6/49. Consequently p+q=55, agreeing with choice A and the key. No statement, choice, or figure contradiction is present.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: LIVE and AoPS Solution 2 are retained in the first route. AoPS Solution 1 groups the same progression sum by its middle bin, Solution 3 reindexes the nested sum, and Solution 4 tabulates the same start-and-spacing calculation; these equivalent computations need no additional method. The shift recurrence adds a useful independently justified route. No shared-bank methods were supplied.
review.annotationCheck: Independence and convergent geometric summation are correctly assessed. Disjoint addition, permutations, and arithmetic-progression terms are appropriate support concepts; recurrence modeling is correctly confined to the alternative method.
review.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is correct; no subject repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The positive parameters enforce distinct positive bins and give a unique progression. Independence yields 8⁻ᵃ8⁻ᵈ per assignment, and exactly six disjoint assignments exist. Both geometric sums equal 1/7, giving the reduced fraction 6/49 and answer 55.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The cited LIVE explanation and AoPS Solution 2 support the parameterization and product sum. The candidate independently explains labeling, uniqueness, and disjointness. The nonofficial source-informed-original classification is accurate.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The parameter choice, factor of six, addition of probabilities, and convergence condition are all explained. The calculation is complete and accessible.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_h140 covers independent products; cnm_h138 covers disjoint addition; cnm_h234 covers the six assignments; cnm_h202 covers the progression; math:infinite-geometric-series covers the convergent sums.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The exact native links for independence, probability addition, permutations, and arithmetic-sequence terms match their uses. The infinite-series node has no accepted CN link.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: S-CP.A.2 partially supports using independence, without testing independence here. S-CP.B.7 supports disjoint addition, while infinite summation exceeds that finite addition step. The narrower F-LE.A.2 and F-BF.A.2 links contribute only arithmetic-sequence structure; full modeling and recursive-form coverage are not demonstrated. No US links are supplied for permutations or infinite series.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All five immediate nodes are supported and sufficiently precise for this route.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Shifting all three labeled placements gives a bijection onto favorable outcomes with minimum bin at least two and scales every probability by 1/8. Minimum-bin-one outcomes total (6/8)(1/7)=3/28. Thus P=P/8+3/28 yields P=6/49 and answer 55.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The references support the progression description and assignment probabilities. The sourceMethod honestly identifies the shift recurrence as newly constructed rather than attributing it to LIVE or AoPS. Its source-informed-original basis is appropriate.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The two classes are exhaustive and disjoint, the shift and inverse are explicit, and the probability scaling is justified. The independent base-class computation makes this a self-contained solution.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: math:recursive-counting-probability fits the justified self-similar probability equation. The other five nodes respectively support independence, geometric summation, progression terms, disjoint addition, and assignments.
